report: Medial betonte Gonarthrose mit in der Belastungszone flächig gemindertem Knorpelbesatz, v.a. tibial, und zentral subchondral ödematösen Veränderungen, ebenfalls tibial führend (exemplarisch 4/18). Fokal hochgradiger chondraler Defekt an der dorsomedialen Femurkondyle mit 11 x 6 mm (ap x ml; 4/23). Innenmeniskus extrudiert stehend bei radiärer Rissbildung nahe der Hinterhornwurzel (4/23)  sowie fraglich horizontaler Rissbildung Pars intermedia/Hinterhorn bei mukoiden Signalalterationen. Zusätzliche Signalalterationen auch des Außenmeniskushinterhorns (5/14). Oberflächliche Chondropathien auch im lateralen femorotibialen Gelenk. Vorderes und hinteres Kreuzband intakt. Lateral betonte Schliffarthrose femoropatellar. Gering Flüssigkeit um das ausgedünnt imponierende MCL, sowie in der Bursa. Mäßiger Gelenkerguss. Zeichen einer chronischen Reizsynovialitis.

Prikaže se hondromalacija III° hrskavice medijalnog tibijalnog platoa kao i hondromalacija
hrskavice lateralnog tibijalnog platoa IV°.
Hondromalacija I° patelarne hrskavice.
Povišen intenzitet signala prednjeg križnog ligamenta u smislu blažih degenerativnih promjena,
održanog kontinuiteta.
Stražnji križni ligament je primjerenih intenziteta signala i održanog kontinuiteta, uz tibijalno
hvatište nalazi se nekoliko ganglion cisti promjera do 4 mm, moguće uslijed deg. promjena
ligamenta i stražnjeg korijena medijalnog meniska.
Vidi se horizontalna ruptura mukoidno degeneriranog lateralnog meniska koja se pruža kroz
stražnji rog, trup i prednji rog.
Znakovi degeneracije medijalnog maniska uz ekstruziju, vidljiva je starija kosa ruptura stražnjeg
roga i parameniscealna cista promjera 4 mm. Opisano odgovara OA promjenama FT zgloba.
Lateralni kolateralni ligament je vretenasto zadebljan pri hvatištu sa lateralni epikondil femura,
prvenstveno entezopatski.
Medijalni kolateralni ligament je primjerenih intenziteta signala, održanog kontinuiteta.
Uredan prikaz tetive popliteusa, iliotibijalnog trakta i pes anserinus.
Tetiva kvadricepsa i patelarni ligament su primjerenih intenziteta signala, održanog kontinuiteta.
Patelarni retinakulumi održani.
Vidi se blaži izljev suprapatelarno.
Burzitis tetive m. semimembranosus.
Ganglion cista uz tetivu m. semitendinosusa promjera 4 mm.
U lateralnom kondolu vidi se T1 i T2 hipointenzivna zona promjera 7 mm, vjerojatno odgovara
ototčiću kompakte.
Difuzno u prikazanim kostima manje T2 hiperinzentivne zone, rekonvezija koštane srži.

MRI OF THE KNEE WITHOUT CONTRAST

HISTORY: Left knee pain. Arthralgia of left lower leg

COMPARISON: None.

PROCEDURE: MRI of the left knee with sagittal, coronal and axial images.

INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST: None

FINDINGS:

Large joint effusion. Trace popliteal cyst     

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES (excluding subchondral marrow):
Moderate subchondral edema in the medial tibial plateau without discrete subchondral fracture, in keeping with osseous stress response.No concerning bone marrow replacing lesion.Tiny tricompartmental marginal osteophytes.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT: 
Medial meniscus: Complete radial tear at junction of posterior horn and root with complex tearing extending into body and medial extrusion. A small portion of the extruded meniscus extends into the posterior-medial tibial recess on coronal series 3 image 16. Small subchondral edema at the adjacent femur is likely reactive.
Cartilage: Full-thickness cartilage loss with small subchondral edema/cystic change involves the majority of femur. Full-thickness and high-grade partial thickness cartilage loss involves majority of the tibial plateau.  

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Intact. No discrete tear.
Cartilage: No high-grade cartilage loss. 

ANTERIOR COMPARTMENT:
Patellar cartilage: Focal high-grade cartilage loss with 3 mm full-thickness delaminating chondral fissure and subchondral edema/cystic change in median ridge. Low-grade partial thickness cartilage loss and medial facet.
Trochlear cartilage: Focal low-grade cartilage loss with heterogeneity in trochlear groove.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Quadriceps tendon: Intact.
Patellar tendon: Intact.
Retinaculum: Intact.
Patellofemoral alignment: Mild lateral patellar tilt. Normal TT-TG. No patella alta.
Hoffa's fat pad: Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Intact.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL): Intact.
Posterolateral corner: Intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Intact.    
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Intact.    

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
Mild insertional semimembranosus tendinosis.. 

SUBCUTANEOUS SOFT TISSUES: 
Nonspecific subcutaneous edema.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for several months.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion. Mild reactive subchondral bone marrow edema at the weightbearing aspect of the medial compartment near the medial joint line. Medial tibiofemoral and patellofemoral compartment marginal osteophytosis.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. Moderate Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tearing of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with dominant radial component at the posterior horn. Superior displacement of a meniscal flap at the posterior horn. Displacement of a meniscal flap into the tibiomeniscal recess. Severe meniscal body extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: High-grade articular cartilage loss of the weightbearing aspect of the joint with confluent areas of full-thickness cartilage loss at the weightbearing medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage irregularity and diffuse low grade cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint with areas of high-grade fissuring.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Confluent full-thickness cartilage loss throughout the patella with subchondral signal changes. Diffuse high-grade articular cartilage loss of the trochlea with regions of full-thickness loss.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Periligamentous edema, likely related to adjacent meniscal pathology.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No lateral patellar tilt. Mild lateral patellar translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 18 mm, borderline elevated.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Severe patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartment osteoarthritis. Complex tearing of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with dominant radial component at the posterior horn. Superior displacement of a small meniscal flap at the posterior horn-root junction. Severe meniscal extrusion.
2.	Moderate knee joint effusion. Moderate leaking Baker's cyst.

Findings:  There is a mild - moderate knee effusion. There is incomplete tearing of the posterior root of the medial meniscus. Mild extrusion of the medial meniscus from the joint is demonstrated. Normal lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is mild thinning of the medial compartment articular cartilage with mild osteophyte formation. Normal lateral compartment articular cartilage. There is severe thinning and loss of the caudal two-thirds of the patellar articular cartilage. The trochlear articular cartilage is relatively preserved.  
Conclusion: Incomplete tearing of the posterior root of the medial meniscus. Mild medial compartment and severe patellar articular cartilage degeneration.
